name: Mai+Chie Kitchen (まいちえキッチン)

claims.text: Operates inside a shared communal kitchen (ミタキシェアキッチン) and bakes/sells wheat products, so shared surfaces and equipment mean flour cross-contact is likely; no dedicated gluten-free prep is claimed.

No tamari/wheat-free soy sauce is specified; standard Japanese shoyu (which contains wheat) should be assumed in seasoned dishes like the tantan noodles and karaage unless the owner confirms otherwise.
Entirely vegan kitchen — no animal products used — so there is no meat/dairy cross-contact risk for plant-based diners.
Vegewel notes English-speaking staff and an English menu are available, which may help a celiac diner ask about ingredients, but no formal allergy protocol is documented.
All-vegan organic concept with some rice-flour (米粉) style baked goods and rice-based Buddha bowls that can be naturally gluten-free if confirmed.
「小麦粉は一切使用しておりません。厨房の調理過程で小麦粉が混入することもありません」 — no wheat flour is used at all, and there is no wheat flour contamination during the kitchen preparation process.
Not applicable — this is a rice-flour bread and sweets bakery with no soy-sauce-based savory dishes; the concern here is wheat flour in baking, which the shop excludes entirely.
Core items such as rice-flour chiffon cakes and florentine contain egg and dairy; no vegan-dedicated equipment or claims are published.
「小麦粉アレルギーの方に配慮しており」 and 「小麦以外の食べ物アレルギーにも対応可能」 — the shop is considerate of wheat-allergy customers and states it can also accommodate non-wheat food allergies.
Fully dedicated 100% rice-flour (グルテンフリー) bakery — no wheat used anywhere and explicit no-cross-contamination claim, making it suitable for celiacs.
Corroborated as a 米粉パン・スイーツ specialty shop by an independent Hiroshima gluten-free roundup.

name: maisondecloth +cafe (メゾンドクロスカフェ)

claims.text: Branded a gluten-free / rice-flour café with no documented wheat items, but no explicit cross-contamination/allergen policy is published — confirm whole-menu wheat-free scope on reservation.
Instagram bio: 「グルテンフリーカフェ/米粉パン」 — gluten-free café / rice-flour bread.
「グルテンフリーのスイーツが楽しめるカフェ」 — a café where you can enjoy gluten-free sweets.

name: ONE EARTH & lovefamcook (ワンアース&ラブファムクック)

claims.text: Wheat burritos (wheat tortilla) and 21-grain sandwich bread are prepared in the same small basement kitchen as any GF-eligible items, creating cross-contact risk; no dedicated GF prep is claimed.

Seasoned Japanese side dishes (e.g. simmered eggplant/potato in the plate sets) are described but no tamari/wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned, so standard wheat-containing soy sauce should be assumed unless confirmed.
Egg and house chicken ham (ハイパワープレート) and yogurt dressing (ライトセット) are used in the same kitchen; vegan dishes exist but are not prepared in a segregated area.
No published statement on celiac/allergy handling; the gluten-free designation comes only from the Vegewel directory tag, not the venue.
All-organic, additive-free, pesticide-free ingredient sourcing with genuine vegan entrees and smoothies, and a Vegewel gluten-free menu tag.

name: Organic cafe & kitchen 喫茶さえき (Organic cafe & kitchen Kissa Saeki)

claims.text: Some savory dishes use wheat-based items — a fu (wheat gluten/seitan) cutlet is on the menu, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat — so gluten-avoiding diners should confirm individual savory dishes; the dessert case is the reliably gluten-free option.
The kitchen also cooks a few non-vegan dishes (free-range chicken karaage), so it is a mixed kitchen rather than fully vegan; plant-based diners rely on items clearly labeled '100% vegan.'
The cafe states its goal is barrier-free dining where food safety is assured for those with allergies and that staff can confidently explain all ingredients with care.
Menu items are clearly marked as '100% vegan food, gluten-free, alcohol-free,' making safe choices easy to identify, and an English menu is available.
All desserts are gluten-free and made with soy milk, including scones and cakes.
Ingredients are organic and local, with no chemical seasonings or GMO foods used in the dishes.
The owner's official site explicitly lists vegan and gluten-free options available alongside the Tex-Mex menu, and describes the room as a small, smoke-free space.

name: アールカフェ キッチネッテ (R Cafe Kitchenette)

claims.text: All cakes are made without wheat flour, offered as a gluten-free sweet option for health-conscious guests.
Health-forward sourcing: grass-fed butter, naturally leavened bread, local Sunatani-dairy milk and seasonal Hiroshima vegetables.

name: 自然食cafe&bar ゆらり（夢楽輪） (Shizenshoku cafe&bar Yurari (Yumerakuwa))

claims.text: The owners state that people with allergies and those who are gluten-free can dine without worry (アレルギーの方も、グルテンフリーの方も気兼ねなく), and dietary restrictions are accommodated, ideally with advance notice.
Explicit vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free menu items are offered.

All ingredients and seasonings are organic and additive-free, with no chemical pesticides, synthetic fertilizers, antibiotics or additives; seasonings like shio-koji are house-made from naturally cultivated rice and sun-dried salt.
The kitchen explicitly aims to let people with allergies, gluten-free and vegan needs all eat together at the same table.
